items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I said, “You let Sinatra do it. You let Dinah Shore.”

ctx.x: Goodnight, Pat. I’ll see you Tuesday. [Pat:] You shall.

Take it easy. I said, “You let Sinatra do it. You let Dinah Shore.” He said, “They didn’t get this much publicity.” He said, “We’ve got a lot of musicians coming in, saying ‘Shaw’s taking the work away from us and giving it to English musicians’.” I got a lot of squawks. Petrillo’s very cynical. One vote, one musician. He’s the guy who made that famous line about, as far as he’s concerned, there’s no difference between the fiddler in the corner tavern and Heifetz. Each was one vote. Hardly a musically encouraging…
So you went off to Spain eventually.
